questions.query: When EEPM1=0 and EEPM0=1 on the ATtiny25/45/85, which EEPROM programming operation is selected, and how long does it take?
questions.reference_answer: Erase Only; 1.8 ms.

questions.query: Which CKSEL fuse setting selects the 32.768 kHz low-frequency crystal oscillator on the ATtiny25/45/85?
questions.reference_answer: CKSEL = 0110.

verbatim_excerpts: setting CKSEL fuses to ‘0110’

questions.query: For the ATtiny25/45/85, which two peripherals should be considered for disabling to save power during sleep, and why?
questions.reference_answer: Disable the ADC before sleeping if unused, because it otherwise remains enabled in all sleep modes; turn off the Brown-out Detector when not needed because it otherwise consumes power in sleep, especially deeper modes.

verbatim_excerpts:
the ADC should be disabled before entering
any sleep mode.
If the Brown-out Detector is not needed in the application, this module should be turned off.

questions.query: How does programming the WDTON fuse change the watchdog initial state and disable behavior on ATtiny25/45/85?
questions.reference_answer: With WDTON unprogrammed, the watchdog starts disabled and can be disabled using a timed sequence; with WDTON programmed, it starts enabled and cannot be disabled (always enabled).

verbatim_excerpts: |Unprogrammed|1|Disabled|Timed sequence|No limitations|
|Programmed|2|Enabled|Always enabled|Timed sequence|

questions.query: What is the register width of TCNT0, OCR0A, and OCR0B in the ATtiny25/45/85 Timer/Counter0?
questions.reference_answer: TCNT0, OCR0A and OCR0B are 8-bit registers.

verbatim_excerpts: The Timer/Counter (TCNT0) and Output Compare Registers (OCR0A and OCR0B) are 8-bit registers.

questions.query: In ATtiny Timer/Counter0 CTC mode, what sets the counter TOP and what event resets TCNT0 to zero?
questions.reference_answer: OCR0A defines TOP and thus counter resolution; TCNT0 is cleared on compare match with OCR0A.

source_evidence.section: 11.7.2 Clear Timer on Compare Match (CTC) Mode
verbatim_excerpts:
The
OCR0A defines the top value for the counter
the counter is cleared to zero when the counter value (TCNT0) matches the OCR0A

questions.query: What prescaler division factor is selected when DTPS11=1 and DTPS10=0 on the ATtiny Timer/Counter1 dead-time prescaler?
questions.reference_answer: The prescaler divides the Timer/Counter1 clock by 4 (4x).

source_evidence.section: 14.1.1 DTPS1 – Timer/Counter1 Dead Time Prescaler Register 1

questions.query: In ATtiny USI three-wire mode, after how many USCK clock pulses are the master/slave data registers interchanged, and which flag can signal completion?
questions.reference_answer: After 8 USCK clocks; the USIOIF counter-overflow interrupt flag can indicate transfer completion.

verbatim_excerpts: after eight USCK clocks
USIOIF, can therefore be used to determine when a transfer is completed

questions.query: How does the master create the START condition on an ATtiny USI two-wire bus, and which flag is set by the slave start detector?
questions.reference_answer: The master drives SDA low while SCL stays high; the slave start detector sets the USISIF flag.

verbatim_excerpts: forcing the SDA low line while keeping the SCL line high
detects the start condition and sets the USISIF Flag

questions.query: When is the USIDC data-output collision flag set in the ATtiny USI, and in which wire mode is it valid?
questions.reference_answer: USIDC is set when bit 7 of the USI Data Register differs from the physical pin level; it is valid only in two-wire mode.

verbatim_excerpts: This bit is logical one when bit 7 in the USI Data Register differs from the physical pin value.

The flag is only valid
when two-wire mode is used.

questions.query: After changing the ADC input channel during ATtiny Free Running mode, which channel is reflected by the next conversion result?
questions.reference_answer: The next result still reflects the previous channel selection; later results reflect the new channel.

verbatim_excerpts:
the next result will reflect the previous channel selection. Subsequent conversions will reflect the
new channel selection.

questions.query: Why can repeatedly changing debugWIRE program breakpoints shorten Flash data retention on ATtiny devices?
questions.reference_answer: Changing a breakpoint requires Flash reprogramming; repeated reprogramming reduces Flash data retention.

verbatim_excerpts: The Flash must be re-programmed each time a Break Point is changed.
The use of Break Points will therefore reduce the Flash Data retention.

questions.query: During an ATtiny Chip Erase, what happens to fuse bits and under what condition is EEPROM preserved?
questions.reference_answer: Fuse bits are not changed; EEPROM contents are preserved if the EESAVE fuse is programmed.

verbatim_excerpts: The Fuse bits are not changed.
The EEPROM memory is preserved during Chip Erase if the EESAVE Fuse is programmed.

questions.query: According to the ATtiny25/45/85 DC characteristics notes, what is the maximum recommended sum of all port output sink currents IOL?
questions.reference_answer: The combined IOL across all ports should not exceed 60 mA.

verbatim_excerpts: The sum of all IOL, for all ports, should not exceed 60 mA.

questions.query: How does the ART Accelerator improve STM32L432xx instruction execution from Flash at high CPU frequencies?
questions.reference_answer: It uses an instruction prefetch queue and a branch cache; performance is described as equivalent to zero Flash wait states up to 80 MHz in the cited CoreMark context.

equivalent to 0 wait state program

questions.query: What single-bit and double-bit error protection does the STM32L432xx embedded Flash ECC provide?
questions.reference_answer: The ECC supports detection and correction of single-bit errors and detection of double-bit errors.

double error detection.

questions.query: What are the STM32L432xx supply voltage ranges for VDD and VDDA, distinguishing ADC/comparator use from DAC/op-amp use?
questions.reference_answer: VDD is 1.71–3.6 V. VDDA is 1.62–3.6 V for ADCs/comparators, and requires at least 1.8 V for DAC/op-amp functions, up to 3.6 V.

VDDA = 1.62 V (ADCs/COMPs) / 1.8 (DAC/OPAMP) to 3.6 V

questions.query: Which ADC input channel digitizes the STM32L432xx internal temperature sensor, and why does it need calibration for accurate temperature measurements?
questions.reference_answer: The internal temperature sensor feeds ADC1_IN17. Device-specific offsets make calibration necessary for good absolute accuracy; ST stores individual factory calibration data in read-only system memory.

questions.query: For the STM32L432xx LSE clock, how does bypass mode differ from using a 32.768 kHz crystal, and what placement practice is recommended for a resonator?
questions.reference_answer: In bypass mode the LSE oscillator is switched off and the input pin operates as a standard GPIO. When using a 32.768 kHz crystal resonator, put it and its load capacitors as close as possible to the oscillator pins to reduce distortion and startup stabilization time.

resonator and the load capacitors have to be placed as close as possible to the oscillator
